title: SEBI's Plan to Help Families Find Investments After You're Gone
description: Unclaimed investments in India are a significant and growing problem, with families often unaware of assets held by deceased relatives. SEBI is working on a c.

faq.q: What is the problem with unclaimed investments?
faq.a: Many financial assets, like bank deposits, mutual funds, and insurance claims, remain unclaimed because families are unaware of them after an investor's death, or due to incomplete documentation. This leads to a loss for legal heirs and a significant pool of dormant capital.

faq.q: How will SEBI's centralised database help?
faq.a: SEBI's proposed database aims to consolidate all an investor's holdings across various SEBI-regulated instruments (like mutual funds and demat accounts) under their PAN. This will create a single point of reference for legal heirs to find and claim assets. [cite: sebi.gov.in]

faq.q: Is a nominee the same as a legal heir?
faq.a: No, a nominee is a person who receives the assets from the institution upon the investor's death, acting as a trustee. The legal heir, as determined by a Will or succession laws, is the ultimate owner of the assets.

faq.q: Why is a Will important even with nominations?
faq.a: A Will legally dictates how your assets should be distributed to your ultimate beneficiaries, overriding nominations in terms of ownership. It ensures your wishes are followed and can prevent family disputes.

faq.q: What should I do if my family doesn't know about my investments?
faq.a: Immediately create a detailed list of all your assets and share its location with a trusted family member. Ensure all nominations are updated and consider drafting a comprehensive Will.

faq.q: Will this database cover all my assets, like bank accounts and property?
faq.a: SEBI's database will primarily cover assets regulated by SEBI, such as mutual funds and shares in demat accounts. Other assets like bank accounts (regulated by RBI) or property will still require separate processes.

based_on.title: Your family may not know where your investments are after you die. SEBI has a plan to help them find them
